Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.orgchart.ui.agenda

Class InvitationSender

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.orgchart.ui.agenda.InvitationSender
public class InvitationSender extends Object
Sends real meeting invitations for an Appointment: it resolves the desktop's default mail account, composes the RFC 5545 METHOD:REQUEST payload with InvitationBuilder, and hands the draft plus its invite.ics attachment to the mail app's existing Jakarta Mail backend through MailSessionManager.

The sender is deliberately UI-agnostic (it never touches Swing or Java 3D) so both the 2D AgendaPanel and the native-3D Agenda3D can share it and the whole send path is unit-testable headlessly with an injected fake MailSessionManager.ServiceFactory. Callers run send(org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.orgchart.ui.agenda.Appointment, java.time.LocalDate, java.util.List<org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.orgchart.ui.agenda.ContactDirectory.ContactInfo>) off the event thread themselves — SMTP is a blocking network round trip.

Credentials. Password handling is exactly the mail app's: a SAVED-mode account's sealed password is recovered silently; an ASK-mode account needs a MailSessionManager.PasswordPrompt installed by the UI (the 2D panel installs one; the 3D app, like Mail3D, does not and reports the manager's user-safe "no password" error instead). No password is ever logged.

    • send

      public int send(Appointment a, LocalDate date, List<ContactDirectory.ContactInfo> invitees) throws MailBackendException
      Invites the given contacts to one occurrence of the appointment and returns how many invitations actually went out.
      Parameters:
      a - the appointment to invite to
      date - the concrete calendar date of the occurrence
      invitees - the resolved contacts (entries without an e-mail are skipped)
      Returns:
      the number of recipients the invitation was sent to
      Throws:
      MailBackendException - with a user-safe message when no invitee has an address, no mail account is configured, the password is unavailable or the SMTP send fails
